The second season of the reimagined science fiction television series ''[[Battlestar Galactica (2004 TV series)|Battlestar Galactica]]'' premiered on [[Syfy|Sci Fi]] in the United States on July 15, 2005, and concluded on March 10, 2006. The season was [[split television season|split]] into two parts, each containing 10 episodes. "Season 2.0" aired from July to September 2005, and "Season 2.5" aired from January to March 2006.

==Production and reception==
Following the success of the 13-episode first season, the Sci-Fi Channel ordered a 20-episode second season on February 23, 2005.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2005/02/23/sci-fi-renews-battlestar-galactica-for-second-season-17883/20050223scifi01/|title=Sci Fi Renews 'Battlestar Galactica' for Second Season|publisher=Sci-Fi Channel|date=February 23, 2005|access-date=June 30, 2011}}</ref> The season premiered in the United States on the Sci-Fi Channel on July 15, 2005, with the UK, Ireland, and Canadian premiere in January 2006. In fall 2005, airing of the second season halted, as it was part of Sci-Fi Channel's standard airing schedule normally used for its ''Stargate'' series, which was to split a 20-episode season into two parts (a "winter season" and a "summer season") to avoid heavy competition with major networks that follow a spring/fall schedule. Universal Home Video took this break as an opportunity to package the episodes aired thus far into a DVD set, calling it "Season 2.0".<ref name="season 2.0">{{cite web|url=http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Battlestar-Galactica/4240|title=Battlestar Galactica - Extras and Box Art for ''Season 2.0''|publisher=TV Shows on DVD|first=David|last=Lambert|date=October 5, 2005|access-date=June 30, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100810143008/http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Battlestar-Galactica/4240|archive-date=August 10, 2010}}</ref> The final episode of the first half, "[[Pegasus (Battlestar Galactica)|Pegasus]]", was originally 15 minutes too long for broadcast, but according to creator Ronald Moore, the production team decided to cut the episode to time rather than pad it out to fill 90 minutes, as this was deemed impractical.<ref>{{cite video|people=D. Moore, Ronald (developer/executive producer)|date=September 19, 2006|title=Battlestar Galactica: Season 2.5 — "Pegasus" commentary|medium=DVD|publisher=Universal Home Video}}</ref> The longer version of "Pegasus" appears on the ''Battlestar Galactica'' Season 2.5 DVD set, which was released in the U.S. on September 19, 2006.<ref name="season 2.5">{{cite web|first=David|last=Lambert|url=http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Battlestar-Galactica/5881|title=Universal Officially Announces ''Battlestar Galactica - Season 2.5''|publisher=TV Shows on DVD|date=June 20, 2006|access-date=May 20, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080531102455/http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Battlestar-Galactica/5881|archive-date=31 May 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[British Sky Broadcasting|Sky]] did not contribute financially to the second season, though UK broadcasts credit the company at the end of every episode.

The second half of season two ("Season 2.5") began airing on January 6, 2006, after a three-month hiatus, during which the Sci-Fi Channel mounted a huge publicity effort. ''Battlestar Galactica'' picked up considerable critical acclaim from the mainstream press, including being named the #1 show of 2005 by ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' magazine,<ref>{{cite magazine|access-date=May 20, 2008|url=http://www.time.com/time/arts/article/0,8599,1141640,00.html|title=Best of 2005: Television|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|date=December 16, 2005|last=Poniewozik|first=James|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080527042310/http://www.time.com/time/arts/article/0%2C8599%2C1141640%2C00.html|archive-date=27 May 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref> and being listed on numerous top ten lists of both 2005 and 2006 by publications such as the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'', ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'', ''[[Newsday]]'' and ''[[TV Guide]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://apps.metacritic.com/tv/bests/2005/|title=Best TV Shows of 2005|publisher=Metacritic|access-date=June 30, 2011| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110714074821/http://apps.metacritic.com/tv/bests/2005/| archive-date= 14 July 2011 | url-status= live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://apps.metacritic.com/tv/bests/2006/|title=Best TV Shows of 2006|publisher=Metacritic|access-date=June 30, 2011| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110714074830/http://apps.metacritic.com/tv/bests/2006/| archive-date= 14 July 2011 | url-status= live}}</ref> The [[American Film Institute]] also named it one of the ten best television shows of 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.afi.com/afiawards/AFIAwards05.aspx|title=AFI Awards 2005|publisher=American Film Institute|access-date=November 28, 2011}}</ref> There was some criticism that a few episodes following "[[Resurrection Ship#Part 2|Resurrection Ship, Part 2]]" were not up to par with previous episodes, such as the episode "[[Black Market (Battlestar Galactica)|Black Market]]", for which even Ron Moore expressed some disdain.<ref>{{cite video|people=D. Moore, Ronald (developer/executive producer)|date=January 27, 2006|title="Black Market" podcast commentary|medium=Podcast|publisher=Sci-Fi Channel}}</ref> Moore stated in his blog that he felt this was a result of the larger workload the series faced with twenty episodes, instead of thirteen in season one. However, episode 15, "[[Scar (Battlestar Galactica)|Scar]]", was thought to bring the series back up to its high level of quality, and subsequent episodes "[[The Captain's Hand]]", "[[Downloaded (Battlestar Galactica)|Downloaded]]", and the two part finale "[[Lay Down Your Burdens]]", were hailed by fans and critics alike. Moore expressed that the longer break between seasons two and three (seven months instead of two) would help to ensure that all episodes were up to the high level of quality that the production team strove to maintain.

==Reception==
===Critical response===
On [[Rotten Tomatoes]], the season has an approval rating of 100% with an average score of 9.5 out of 10 based on 12 reviews. The website's critical consensus reads, "In its second season, ''Battlestar Galatica'' doubles down on the series' high-minded themes and satisfyingly complex storylines."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/battlestar-galactica/s02 |title=Battlestar Galactica: Season 2 |website=Rotten Tomatoes |accessdate=November 12, 2021}}</ref>

==Home video releases==
Season 2.0 and 2.5 were released on DVD in region 1 on December 20, 2005,<ref name="season 2.0"/> and September 19, 2006,<ref name="season 2.5"/> respectively. The complete second season was released on [[Blu-ray Disc]] in region 1 on April 6, 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Battlestar-Galactica-Season-2-Blu-ray/13204|title=Battlestar Galactica - Spin Up Your Blu-ray Drives: Season 2 Jumps to High-Def!|first=David|last=Lambert|publisher=TV Shows on DVD|date=January 12, 2010|access-date=June 30, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100526082100/http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/Battlestar-Galactica-Season-2-Blu-ray/13204|archive-date=May 26, 2010}}</ref> The complete second season was released on DVD in region 2 on August 28, 2006<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B000GLKNRI/|title=Battlestar Galactica: Season 2|date=August 28, 2006 |publisher=Amazon.co.uk|access-date=June 30, 2011}}</ref> and in region 4 on April 4, 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ezydvd.com.au/item.zml/792297|title=Battlestar Galactica (2004) - Season 2.0|publisher=EzyDVD|access-date=June 30, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110303030541/http://www.ezydvd.com.au/item.zml/792297|archive-date=March 3, 2011}}</ref>

The Season 2.0 DVD set includes the first 10 episodes of season two. Special features on the set include creator [[Ronald D. Moore]]'s podcast commentaries for 7 of the 10 episodes; a podcast for "Fragged" was not recorded, while the podcasts for "Flight of the Phoenix" and "Pegasus" were not recorded in time for the DVDs, but are available on the official website. Also included are deleted scenes for 9 episodes and a sneak peek promo for the second half of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/reviews/Battlestar-Galactica-Season-20/5290|title=Battlestar Galactica - Season 2.0 Review|first=Gord|last=Lacey|publisher=TV Shows on DVD|date=December 20, 2005|access-date=June 30, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100726132609/http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/reviews/Battlestar-Galactica-Season-20/5290|archive-date=July 26, 2010}}</ref> The Season 2.5 DVD set includes the last 10 episodes of season two, plus the extended hour-long version of "Pegasus". Special features include Moore's podcast commentaries for all 10 episodes; he is joined by writers [[David Weddle]] and [[Bradley Thompson]] on "Scar", his wife Terry Dresbach on "Lay Down Your Burdens, Part 1" and executive producer [[David Eick]] on "Lay Down Your Burdens, Part 2". Moore and Eick provide audio commentary for the extended version of "Pegasus", a commentary specifically produced for the DVD. Also included are deleted scenes for 8 episodes, 7 of David Eick's videoblogs, and a collection of the R&D logos that appear at the end of each episode.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/reviews/Battlestar-Galactica-Season-25/5942|title=Battlestar Galactica - Season 2.5 Review|first=Gord|last=Lacey|publisher=TV Shows on DVD|date=September 24, 2006|access-date=June 30, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100724115201/http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/reviews/Battlestar-Galactica-Season-25/5942|archive-date=July 24, 2010}}</ref>
